question: How does reference-selected mapping behave when generated forms share a length and their slot distributions share probability mass?
outcome: Twelve fresh matched twenty-symbol systems give 192 conditions. At reference size 400, selected recovery is 24/24 separated, 22/24 same-length zero shared mass, 22/24 mass .35 and 16/24 mass .70. At size 40 the counts are 10/24, 8/24, 2/24 and 0/24. Supplied form labels improve same-record recovery in several conditions. All 9,202 primary checks and 384 dual certificates pass; thirty linear ties have sixty exact witnesses.
challenge: Equalizing length adds slots, so that contrast changes record content. Small references and overlapping role distributions can favor wrong objectives; all failed returned mappings score above the true map under their fitted objectives.
remedy: Preserve matched uniforms and complete parameters, isolate shared-mass contrasts among six-slot forms, compare supplied labels on identical records, independently replay choices/counts/scores and retain exact ties, paired system intervals and optimization diagnostics.
retry_when: A frozen latent-form estimator, new independently observed record class, larger reference or uncertain-boundary control changes the mapping information.
